reason: I'll follow the rubble world's encounter with the giant and see whether it stays bound to its sun.
expectation: The giant's gravity may redirect the world, possibly ejecting it from the system.

alternatives.reason: The passing star's effect on the distant ice is also interesting, but I want to follow the rubble world first.

effect: The giant sent the intact world outward but did not eject it; the passing star may change its orbit further.
reaction: I was surprised it remained bound after the encounter.
reason: Follow the rubble world into its encounter with the passing star.
expectation: The star's gravity may free the world from its sun, though it could instead alter its orbit or capture it.

alternatives.reason: The ice's encounter also advances a goal, but I want to finish following the rubble world first.

effect: The passing star freed the intact rubble world without capturing it, completing that goal.
reaction: It's striking that the world remains together despite losing its sun.
reason: The ice's encounter is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: Some distant ice may be captured by the passing star, though its final orbit is uncertain.

effect: The passing star captured a separate portion of the ice, while most remained with the original sun; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast between captured ice and the escaping rubble world made the role of encounter geometry clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the rubble world past the star was most worthwhile: it lost its sun but remained intact and within the galaxy.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final ice encounter was the only remaining combination, so choosing it involved little decision-making, although its explanation was useful.

surprise.text: The giant sent the rubble world far outward without ejecting or breaking it.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each encounter had a clear gravitational purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the sunless world and captured ice further, especially after their different outcomes in the same encounter.
